title: Chapter XXVII
summary: Rochester explains that his father and brother arranged his Jamaican marriage for money while concealing hereditary illness, and that Bertha's condition and conduct drove him to confinement, wandering, and mistresses. He asks Jane to live with him in France as his true partner, arguing that the existing marriage is only a legal shell. Jane still loves him intensely but sees that becoming his mistress would destroy the self he loves. Because principles matter precisely under temptation, she refuses. After a dream commands her to flee, she secretly leaves Thornfield with almost nothing.
events: Rochester narrates his arranged marriage, Bertha's decline, her confinement with Grace Poole, and his subsequent wandering.
He proposes that Jane live with him abroad despite the legal marriage.
Jane rejects the proposal because obedience would violate her conscience and ultimately her self-respect.
Jane departs before dawn and takes a coach far from Thornfield.

characters.name: Jane Eyre
characters.development: Chooses conscience and durable self-respect over immediate love, security, and the chance to rescue Rochester.

characters.name: Edward Rochester
characters.development: Offers a compelling account of victimization but still asks Jane to bear the moral cost of his attempt to escape it.

characters.name: Bertha Mason Rochester
characters.development: Her history is supplied almost entirely through Rochester's hostile account, which explains his misery without undoing her legal existence.

threads.text: Rochester's past error and the conventional obstacle are disclosed as his existing marriage to Bertha.
Jane's earlier promise to obey only in what is right determines her refusal.
Jane enters the world alone, homeless, and nearly penniless.
Separation is necessary before Jane and Rochester could ever meet on genuinely free terms.
